subject: QBR prep: capacity scenarios + GPU unit-econ asklist
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: QBR prep: capacity scenarios + GPU unit-econ asklist

Team —

We need a concise packet for next week’s QBR that focuses on infra capacity scenarios and unit economics. Executive asks are:
- Three capacity scenarios (Conservative / Target / Surge) with corresponding GPU count, expected utilization, and monthly spend.
- Unit economics summary: $/GPU-hour, effective $/1K tokens under current batching/caching assumptions, and sensitivity to utilization +/-10/20%.
- Short list of operational levers (batching window, prefix cache hit target, quantization profile) and estimated savings per lever.

Requesting the following by EOD tomorrow so I can compile:
1) Laura — updated capacity model (spreadsheet) with scenario sheets and a short note on assumptions.
2) Vivek — current month actual GPU utilization by pool + forecast impact if we enable the proposed 50ms batching window.
3) Rishi — risk notes: any capacity constraints, perf regressions, or SLA exposures for the Surge scenario.
4) Karthik — quick run of the amortized infra cost across Dedicated vs Hosted for the Target scenario and a recommendation.

Attach numbers, a 1-page slide or bullet summary, and call out any asks for exec decisions (e.g., temporary burst credit, approval for reserved nodes). I’ll also include a short external-facing blurb for concerned customers (Acme Retail) about what to expect if we need to shift routing during surge.

Thanks — keep it tight.

— Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Infrastructure & Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR prep: capacity scenarios + GPU unit-econ asklist

Markus —

Uploading the capacity model: attached as qbr_capacity_model_v2.xlsx and linked the working sheet (https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1QBR-capacity-sim). High level notes:
- Conservative: keep current committed Dedicated pools + 10% buffer (assumes no new major deals). Peak GPU count: 96. Ave util: 48%. Monthly GPU spend (incl. infra overhead): $320k.
- Target: assume 2 new mid-market deals, small growth in embedding workloads. Peak GPU count: 132. Ave util: 62%. Monthly GPU spend: $445k.
- Surge: +40% traffic (holiday/promo). Peak GPU count: 188. Ave util: 74% but several pools hit hot-spoting; monthly GPU spend: $640k.

Assumptions tab includes token mix (chat vs single-turn), average sequence lengths, and effective batch sizes. I added a sensitivity matrix for utilization +/-10/20% and a sheet with the estimated effect of enabling prefix KV cache at 30%/50% hit rates.

Attachments: batching_sim_results-summary.pdf (short notes from infra sim runs).

If helpful I can export a 1-slide summary.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR prep: capacity scenarios + GPU unit-econ asklist

Quick datapoints from infra metrics:
- Current month observed utilization by pool (avg across 7d): Pool-A 55%, Pool-B 47%, Pool-C 38%. Weighted avg: 50.4%.
- Enabling 50ms batching window in the inference router (baseline sim): increases effective batch size by ~1.8x for chat workloads and yields ~22% reduction in tokens per GPU-hour for chat-dominant routes. Net projected monthly saving for Target scenario: ~$72k.
- Prefix KV cache at 50% hit reduces backend compute by ~15% on chat-heavy routes; combined with batching gives ~33% token-cost reduction in that cohort.

Risks: latency tail increases for very short queries; recommend a per-route SLO for tail p99 and a short canary (10% traffic) for 48 hours.

I attached the sim summary (batching_sim_results-summary.pdf).

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Elaine Sorrento <elaine.sorrento@acme-retail.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acme-retail.com
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR prep: capacity scenarios + GPU unit-econ asklist

Markus / Laura —

Thanks for the heads-up and the model you shared. A couple quick asks from our side ahead of the QBR:
1) Can you provide the projected impact on response latency for our primary chat route under the Surge scenario if batching and prefix-caching are enabled? We need to confirm it stays within our SLA of 350ms median / 900ms p99.
2) If we move a portion of our traffic to the Hosted fallback during peak, what billing delta should we expect vs Dedicated (ballpark per 1M tokens)?

Procurement: we may need a temp addendum for burst capacity if Surge looks likely — copying them to coordinate paperwork.

— Elaine
Elaine Sorrento
Head of AI Products
Acme Retail
